Title: The 5 Best Recipes of 2023
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8
For Allrecipes' inaugural Best Recipes contest, we tasked our readers, editors, and a panel of expert judges to name the best recipes of the year.
The internet at large likes to throw around the word "best" a lot. This is the _best_ cheeseburger; this is the _best_ way to store blueberries; this is the _best_ way to cut an onion. We get the appeal! When you're deciding between multiple recipes or techniques, why wouldn't you want the best?
But there's just one problem: Who, exactly, gets to decide what qualifies as the best? Who gets to say what recipe is better than another? This year, for the first time ever, we're letting our editors, readers, and a panel of expert judges make the call. For Allrecipes' inaugural **Best Recipes**competition, we pitted 50 recipes against each other to find the "best" recipe in five different categories: bacon, cheese, chicken, potatoes, and chocolate. We whittled down the list, we consulted our readers (almost 20,000 members of our community weighed in!), we ate our way through plates of chicken Parmesan and rich chocolate pie, and we found our champions.
The five winning recipes below are the result of many months of research culminating in a cook-off at our test kitchen in Birmingham. When we say these recipes are "the best" for 2023, you can rest assured that it's true.
Dotdash Meredith Design

## How We Decided the Best Recipes of 2023
We took a three-prong approach to finding our best recipes for 2023. In the first phase, our editors determined the five ingredient-based categories, and then chose 10 recipes per category that we felt represented what our community is making right now on Allrecipes—whether that’s something highly rated, brimming with comments on Instagram, or very much in the zeitgeist in 2023. It didn't matter when the recipes were published.
In the second phase, we kicked off a month-long campaign where we asked our readers to vote for their favorite recipes in each category. We had an incredible 111,554 votes from 17,255 voters (with a $1000 cash prize for voting).
The top two recipes in each category went to a cook-off in our test kitchen in Birmingham, Alabama where our panel of judges—Carrie Boyd, Elizabeth Heiskell, and Dakari Akored—tried all 10 recipes, gave their notes, deliberated amongst themselves, and declared one winner per category.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Meet the Judges
For our cook-off in Birmingham, we brought in three top-tier judges to make the final call on the best recipes of 2023. Let's meet the team!
*   **Elizabeth Heiskell**: Heiskell is a _The Today Show_ Food Contributor and has appeared on both _The Kitchen_ and _Chopped_. She's also the best-selling cookbook author of _What Can I Bring_, _The Southern Living Party Cookbook_, and _Come On Over_. She lives in Oxford, Mississippi where she runs her catering company, Elizabeth Heiskell Catering.  
*   **Dakari Akorede**: Akorede is an Allrecipes' Allstar, a football fan, and a BBQ expert. He lives in Atlanta and works as a private chef and teacher.  
*   **Carrie Boyd**: Boyd is the Editorial Director for _Allrecipes_ magazine. She has more than a decade of experience in national food and lifestyle media and content creation. In another life, she created custom, branded content for national brands; and worked in various FOH and BOH jobs in the hospitality industry. She lives in Iowa.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## The Best Recipes 2023 Cook-Off
When it comes to the vibe of our cook-off in Birmingham on July 26, think: _Top Chef_ meets the home cook. In typical TV fashion, our judges sat on a long table, with fork and pen in hand, ready to eat and take notes. Our test kitchen chefs made and served our judges each recipe while telling them a little bit about the history of the dish on the site. Allrecipes is built on the recipes from our contributors, so it was a joy to hear about the cook behind the dish, and when it was published on our site (a couple were from 1999!). The judges in turn tried each recipe, gave their notes, and voted on the ultimate winner. Here's how the whole thing shook out.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Bacon: Not Just a Morning Hero
**The Contenders**: **Bacon-Wrapped Jalapeño Poppers** vs. **Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole**
Our test kitchen chefs, Jasmine Smith and Julia Levy, made and served both of these recipes to our judges. The poppers had thick-cut bacon wrapped around the outside of the pepper, while the casserole has bacon throughout and on top of the dish. The judges swooned over the poppers, and Akorede said the recipe was "savory, salty, with just a small twinge of heat". But ultimately, **the casserole reigned supreme**. Boyd described it as “the perfect marriage" of an egg casserole and a hot dish. “I have no notes here,” she said, "10/10."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Potatoes: The Queen of Comfort
**The Contenders**: **Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes** vs. **Creamy au Gratin Potatoes**
For our potato category, our test kitchen pros Amanda Stanfield and Catherine Jesse made and served our judges. The baked potatoes were a twice-baked potato filled with bacon, cheddar, sour cream, and green onions. The gratin potatoes used thinly-sliced potatoes as the base. The judges thought that the potatoes in the gratin were perfectly cooked, but Akorede thought the "onions were too sharp." **The baked potato stole the show**. "This [recipe] makes me think about home," Akorede said.
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Cheese: The Secret to Making Everything Better
**The Contenders**: **VELVEETA Down-Home Macaroni and Cheese** vs. **Cheddar Bay Biscuits**
Stanfield and Jesse came back to make and serve the recipes for the cheese category to our judges. The macaroni and cheese used two kinds of cheeses for superior creaminess—VELVEETA and cheddar. And the Red Lobster copycat biscuits used grated cheddar to impart cheesiness throughout. While the judges thought the biscuits were "light and savory" they also thought they were a tad bit dry. **The macaroni and cheese**, on the other hand, was "creamy and delicious" according to Heiskell, making it our #1 cheese recipe of 2023.
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Chicken: A Kitchen Bedrock
**The Contenders**: **Chicken Parmesan** vs. **Juicy Roast Chicken**
Our test kitchen chefs, Nicole Hopper and Tricia Stuedeman, made and served our judges for the chicken category. The roast chicken is a fuss-free recipe with superior results, and the chicken Parmesan uses a mixture of panko and Parmesan for ultimate crispiness. Heiskell thought the roast chicken was incredibly juicy. "It's easy to hide behind a dry wing or thigh, but you can't do that with the breast," she said. **But Boyd and Akorede preferred the chicken Parmesan, making it our winner**. Akorede said it was a "great dish" and that the chicken was "perfectly fried."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Chocolate: The Sweetest Way to End the Day
**The Contenders: Rich Chocolate Truffle Pie** vs. **One Bowl Chocolate Cake**
Stuedeman and Hopper also made and served the chocolate recipes to our judges. The cake uses unsweetened cocoa powder, while the pie utilized semisweet chocolate chips and a chocolate cookie crumb crust. Heiskell thought the cake was a "lovely rich and moist cake," **but it didn't hold a candle to the pie**. Akorede's eyes rolled to the back of his head while declaring that the pie was "absolutely phenomenal."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Design

_**Best Recipes 2023**: Allrecipes asked our readers and a panel of judges to help us find the best recipe in five different categories: bacon, chicken, potatoes, cheese, and chocolate._**_See the full list of winners here_**_, and read more about the best chicken recipe below._
We have over 5,000 chicken recipes on Allrecipes—so it's safe to say our community loves its poultry. To find the best chicken recipe of the year, our editors looked at our library and chose 10 recipes that were beloved by our readers and/or were popular on the internet right now. Then, our readers voted on their favorite recipe, and the top two went to a cook-off in Birmingham where our judges—Carrie Boyd, Elizabeth Heiskell, and Dakari Akorede—chose a champion.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The Best Chicken Recipe of 2023 Is "Perfectly Fried"
## Meet the Two Contenders
*   **Chicken Parmesan**: This recipe was published by Chef John on June 6, 2012. It has over 3,200 reviews with a 4.7-star rating. It's also our top chicken recipe of the past 12 months. Test kitchen pro Nicole Hopper told our judges that this recipe is "very straightforward" but that it's a less-saucy version than some might be used to. Hopper said this was great because it helped avoid that dreaded soggy-bottom chicken. She also notes that the recipe uses three kinds of cheese: mozzarella, provolone, and Parmesan.

*   **Juicy Roast Chicken**: ROBINROCKINGBIRD published this recipe on May 4, 2005. It has over 3,100 reviews with a 4.7-star rating, and it was our third most popular chicken recipe of the past 12 months. Our test kitchen pro, Tricia Stuedeman, says this recipe lives up to its name—it's ultra juicy. The chicken also roasts at one temperature the entire time, making it pretty fuss-free.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The Best Chicken Recipe of 2023 Is "Perfectly Fried"
## What the Judges Had to Say
*   **Chicken Parmesan**: Akorede loved this recipe immediately. "It's a great dish, perfectly fried chicken with the added sweetness of the sauce and cheese," he said. Boyd thought the jarred sauce was "a bit underwhelming" but that she "loved the crispy texture" overall. Heiskell thought the chicken breast "was a little too dry."

*   **Juicy Roast Chicken**: The judges were impressed by how juicy this chicken was. "It's easy to hide behind a dry wing or thigh, but you can't do that with the breast," explained Heiskell. "The seasoning on the outside definitely got all the way through, she continued. Akorede thought the recipe called for too much onion powder, but he was impressed by the crispiness of the skin. Boyd sayid that the chicken was definitely juicy, "but basic."
Dotdash Meredith Food Studio

# The Best Chicken Recipe of 2023 Is "Perfectly Fried"
## And the Winner Is...
As the judges were deliberating, Heiskell had some concerns about whether or not the panko-Parmesan was doing all of the heavy lifting for the Chicken Parmesan. Was it really a fair matchup? Because of this, she decided to cast her vote for the Juicy Roasted Chicken, but the other two judges—Boyd and Akorede—went for the **Chicken Parmesan**, making it our winning recipe for 2023.

_**Best Recipes 2023**: Allrecipes asked our readers and a panel of judges to help us find the best recipe in five different categories: bacon, chicken, potatoes, cheese, and chocolate._**_See the full list of winners here_**_, and read more about the best cheese recipe below._
Cheese is the literal magic sauce in our mac and cheese, the tour de force in our enchiladas, and the wind beneath (or on top of) our pizza. That's why when we attempted to find the best cheese recipe for Allrecipes' Best Recipes 2023 competition, we took the task very seriously. After our editors whittled down our cheesiest recipes—based on what our readers love and trending dishes—our readers voted on the top 10. The top two recipes went to a cook-off in Birmingham where our judges—Carrie Boyd, Elizabeth Heiskell, and Dakari Akorede—chose the winner. Not to be cheesy or anything, but we truly love the #1 dish.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The #1 Cheese Recipe of 2023 Is the Creamiest Thing You'll Eat All Year
## Meet the Two Contenders
*   **VELVEETA Down-Home Macaroni and Cheese:**This recipe is from VELVEETA Cheese, and was originally published on April 15, 2013. It has 150 reviews with a 4.5-star rating. It made the running for our Best Recipes 2023 contest because it was voted the best mac and cheese recipe in a recent taste test. Our test kitchen pro Amanda Stanfield, says this recipe gets its creaminess from a mix of VELVEETA cheese and cheddar. But what really puts this recipe over the edge is the buttery, crushed Ritz cracker that you add on top of the pasta before baking.

*   **Cheddar Bay Biscuits:**This recipe comes from Cookie, and was first published on April 4, 1999. The biscuits have over 1,300 reviews with a 4.6-star rating. Our test kitchen pro, Catherine Jesse, says this Red Lobster copycat is filled with lots of cheddar cheese, garlic powder, butter, flour, and a few other seasonings.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The #1 Cheese Recipe of 2023 Is the Creamiest Thing You'll Eat All Year
## What the Judges Had to Say
*   **VELVEETA Down-Home Macaroni and Cheese:** Boyd said this macaroni and cheese was "creamy, cheesy, and so tasty!" And that she loved the buttery Ritz crackers on top. Akorede agreed with Boyd, but thought the dish could use a "pop of Parm to offset the VELVEETA." Heiskell said that the recipe was very "creamy and delicious."

*   **Cheddar Bay Biscuits:**Akorede described this recipe as "garlic butter heaven," and Heiskell said the biscuits were "light and savory." Boyd said they were a little dry, but that they were "exactly what I wanted and expected." Akorede also agreed with Boyd that the biscuits were a bit dry, and suggested more butter.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The #1 Cheese Recipe of 2023 Is the Creamiest Thing You'll Eat All Year
## And the Winner Is...
Ultimately, **VELVEETA Down-Home Macaroni and Cheese** took the throne for 2023. "You can't compete in a cheese category against macaroni and cheese, I'm sorry, you just can't," says Heiskell. "You're not wrong," says Boyd.

# The Best Bacon Recipe on Our Site This Year, According to Fans
_**Best Recipes 2023**: Allrecipes asked our readers and a panel of judges to help us find the best recipe in five different categories: bacon, chicken, potatoes, cheese, and chocolate._**_See the full list of winners here_**_, and read more about the best bacon recipe below._
For the first time ever, Allrecipes has itself a definitive _best_ bacon recipe.
Back in June, the Allrecipes team took on the challenge of finding the best recipe on our site. But, as the largest food site on the internet with over 55,000 recipes, we decided it was only right to break the recipes into categories (I mean, how can you possibly pit the Best Chocolate Chip Cookie against Creamy au Gratin Potatoes?). So, the five contending categories were: bacon, potatoes, cheese, chicken, and chocolate. We gave you 10 community-favorite recipe options for each category, then asked you to vote on the best of each.
In the bacon bracket, the recipes ranged from corn dishes to cabbage dishes, from pasta salads to savory snacks. But, to be the very best, this dish had to be salty, satisfying, and bring full-force bacon flavor. Thanks to your votes, we were able to narrow the bacon recipe pool down to two delicious finalists. It was up to our judges—Carrie Boyd, Elizabeth Heiskell, and Dakari Akorede—to pick the winner.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The Best Bacon Recipe on Our Site This Year, According to Fans
## Meet the Two Contenders
In our inaugural Best Recipe Cook-Off, we had two of our talented recipe testers, Jasmine Smith and Julia Levy, battle it out between the top two bacon recipes.
**Bacon-Wrapped Jalapeño Poppers**: This recipe comes to us from community member videogator, and was first published on July 25, 2013. The flavorful jalapeño poppers are crispy on the outside, and soft and creamy in the center. Stuffed with two kinds of cheese (cream cheese and sharp Cheddar), the poppers deliver layers of savory, spicy flavor in every bite.
"Wrapped with bacon, these are absolutely the best," says user R Vicente.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
They're easy to make (only four ingredients!), perfectly balanced, and exactly what you want to find on the appetizer table. It doesn't matter if you bake them or grill them—these bacon-wrapped peppers will add a delicious kick to any get-together.
**Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole**: This breakfast casserole from SPezz was first published on November 16, 2014. It's made for morning comfort, combining every element of your favorite breakfast in one flavorful bite. It's savory, satisfying, and best of all, simple.
“I put this together in what felt like 5 minutes,” recipe tester Julia said.
This 5-ingredient wonder can be customized with veggies, herbs, or hot sauce, and it’ll still turn out delicious every time.
Peyton Beckwith/Dotdash Meredith

# The Best Bacon Recipe on Our Site This Year, According to Fans
## What the Judges Had to Say
*   **Bacon-Wrapped Jalapeño Poppers**: "Yummmm, exactly what I want tailgating," says Boyd. "The cheddar addition is tasty and different." Akorede agreed, saying "The contrast—the cream cheese in conjunction with the bacon—you can’t beat it." Heiskell said although the peppers were roasted perfectly, bacon was the star of this dish: "It was the first thing I saw."

*   **Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole:** “You know, I make a breakfast casserole, and I have for years, but I have to say, this one is on a whole 'nother level. This has got everything—it has the bacon, and then the tater tots! I mean, come on! Who does that?,” raved Heiskell. Boyd said it was “the perfect marriage” of an egg casserole and a hot dish. “I have no notes here,” she said, "10/10."
Peyton Beckwith/Dotdash Meredith

# The Best Bacon Recipe on Our Site This Year, According to Fans
## And the Winner Is...
The **Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole**!

For Allrecipes' inaugural Best Recipes contest, we tasked our readers, editors, and a panel of expert judges to name the best recipes of the year.
The internet at large likes to throw around the word "best" a lot. This is the _best_ cheeseburger; this is the _best_ way to store blueberries; this is the _best_ way to cut an onion. We get the appeal! When you're deciding between multiple recipes or techniques, why wouldn't you want the best?
But there's just one problem: Who, exactly, gets to decide what qualifies as the best? Who gets to say what recipe is better than another? This year, for the first time ever, we're letting our editors, readers, and a panel of expert judges make the call. For Allrecipes' inaugural **Best Recipes**competition, we pitted 50 recipes against each other to find the "best" recipe in five different categories: bacon, cheese, chicken, potatoes, and chocolate. We whittled down the list, we consulted our readers (almost 20,000 members of our community weighed in!), we ate our way through plates of chicken Parmesan and rich chocolate pie, and we found our champions.
The five winning recipes below are the result of many months of research culminating in a cook-off at our test kitchen in Birmingham. When we say these recipes are "the best" for 2023, you can rest assured that it's true.
Dotdash Meredith Design
texts.1:
## How We Decided the Best Recipes of 2023
We took a three-prong approach to finding our best recipes for 2023. In the first phase, our editors determined the five ingredient-based categories, and then chose 10 recipes per category that we felt represented what our community is making right now on Allrecipes—whether that’s something highly rated, brimming with comments on Instagram, or very much in the zeitgeist in 2023. It didn't matter when the recipes were published.
In the second phase, we kicked off a month-long campaign where we asked our readers to vote for their favorite recipes in each category. We had an incredible 111,554 votes from 17,255 voters (with a $1000 cash prize for voting).
The top two recipes in each category went to a cook-off in our test kitchen in Birmingham, Alabama where our panel of judges—Carrie Boyd, Elizabeth Heiskell, and Dakari Akored—tried all 10 recipes, gave their notes, deliberated amongst themselves, and declared one winner per category.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
texts.2:
## Meet the Judges
For our cook-off in Birmingham, we brought in three top-tier judges to make the final call on the best recipes of 2023. Let's meet the team!
*   **Elizabeth Heiskell**: Heiskell is a _The Today Show_ Food Contributor and has appeared on both _The Kitchen_ and _Chopped_. She's also the best-selling cookbook author of _What Can I Bring_, _The Southern Living Party Cookbook_, and _Come On Over_. She lives in Oxford, Mississippi where she runs her catering company, Elizabeth Heiskell Catering.  
*   **Dakari Akorede**: Akorede is an Allrecipes' Allstar, a football fan, and a BBQ expert. He lives in Atlanta and works as a private chef and teacher.  
*   **Carrie Boyd**: Boyd is the Editorial Director for _Allrecipes_ magazine. She has more than a decade of experience in national food and lifestyle media and content creation. In another life, she created custom, branded content for national brands; and worked in various FOH and BOH jobs in the hospitality industry. She lives in Iowa.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
texts.3:
## The Best Recipes 2023 Cook-Off
When it comes to the vibe of our cook-off in Birmingham on July 26, think: _Top Chef_ meets the home cook. In typical TV fashion, our judges sat on a long table, with fork and pen in hand, ready to eat and take notes. Our test kitchen chefs made and served our judges each recipe while telling them a little bit about the history of the dish on the site. Allrecipes is built on the recipes from our contributors, so it was a joy to hear about the cook behind the dish, and when it was published on our site (a couple were from 1999!). The judges in turn tried each recipe, gave their notes, and voted on the ultimate winner. Here's how the whole thing shook out.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
texts.4:
## Bacon: Not Just a Morning Hero
**The Contenders**: **Bacon-Wrapped Jalapeño Poppers** vs. **Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole**
Our test kitchen chefs, Jasmine Smith and Julia Levy, made and served both of these recipes to our judges. The poppers had thick-cut bacon wrapped around the outside of the pepper, while the casserole has bacon throughout and on top of the dish. The judges swooned over the poppers, and Akorede said the recipe was "savory, salty, with just a small twinge of heat". But ultimately, **the casserole reigned supreme**. Boyd described it as “the perfect marriage" of an egg casserole and a hot dish. “I have no notes here,” she said, "10/10."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
texts.5:
## Potatoes: The Queen of Comfort
**The Contenders**: **Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes** vs. **Creamy au Gratin Potatoes**
For our potato category, our test kitchen pros Amanda Stanfield and Catherine Jesse made and served our judges. The baked potatoes were a twice-baked potato filled with bacon, cheddar, sour cream, and green onions. The gratin potatoes used thinly-sliced potatoes as the base. The judges thought that the potatoes in the gratin were perfectly cooked, but Akorede thought the "onions were too sharp." **The baked potato stole the show**. "This [recipe] makes me think about home," Akorede said.
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
texts.6:
## Cheese: The Secret to Making Everything Better
**The Contenders**: **VELVEETA Down-Home Macaroni and Cheese** vs. **Cheddar Bay Biscuits**
Stanfield and Jesse came back to make and serve the recipes for the cheese category to our judges. The macaroni and cheese used two kinds of cheeses for superior creaminess—VELVEETA and cheddar. And the Red Lobster copycat biscuits used grated cheddar to impart cheesiness throughout. While the judges thought the biscuits were "light and savory" they also thought they were a tad bit dry. **The macaroni and cheese**, on the other hand, was "creamy and delicious" according to Heiskell, making it our #1 cheese recipe of 2023.
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
texts.7:
## Chicken: A Kitchen Bedrock
**The Contenders**: **Chicken Parmesan** vs. **Juicy Roast Chicken**
Our test kitchen chefs, Nicole Hopper and Tricia Stuedeman, made and served our judges for the chicken category. The roast chicken is a fuss-free recipe with superior results, and the chicken Parmesan uses a mixture of panko and Parmesan for ultimate crispiness. Heiskell thought the roast chicken was incredibly juicy. "It's easy to hide behind a dry wing or thigh, but you can't do that with the breast," she said. **But Boyd and Akorede preferred the chicken Parmesan, making it our winner**. Akorede said it was a "great dish" and that the chicken was "perfectly fried."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
texts.8:
## Chocolate: The Sweetest Way to End the Day
**The Contenders: Rich Chocolate Truffle Pie** vs. **One Bowl Chocolate Cake**
Stuedeman and Hopper also made and served the chocolate recipes to our judges. The cake uses unsweetened cocoa powder, while the pie utilized semisweet chocolate chips and a chocolate cookie crumb crust. Heiskell thought the cake was a "lovely rich and moist cake," **but it didn't hold a candle to the pie**. Akorede's eyes rolled to the back of his head while declaring that the pie was "absolutely phenomenal."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Design

# The Best Chicken Recipe of 2023 Is "Perfectly Fried"
## Meet the Two Contenders
*   **Chicken Parmesan**: This recipe was published by Chef John on June 6, 2012. It has over 3,200 reviews with a 4.7-star rating. It's also our top chicken recipe of the past 12 months. Test kitchen pro Nicole Hopper told our judges that this recipe is "very straightforward" but that it's a less-saucy version than some might be used to. Hopper said this was great because it helped avoid that dreaded soggy-bottom chicken. She also notes that the recipe uses three kinds of cheese: mozzarella, provolone, and Parmesan.

*   **Juicy Roast Chicken**: ROBINROCKINGBIRD published this recipe on May 4, 2005. It has over 3,100 reviews with a 4.7-star rating, and it was our third most popular chicken recipe of the past 12 months. Our test kitchen pro, Tricia Stuedeman, says this recipe lives up to its name—it's ultra juicy. The chicken also roasts at one temperature the entire time, making it pretty fuss-free.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
texts.5:
# The Best Chicken Recipe of 2023 Is "Perfectly Fried"
## What the Judges Had to Say
*   **Chicken Parmesan**: Akorede loved this recipe immediately. "It's a great dish, perfectly fried chicken with the added sweetness of the sauce and cheese," he said. Boyd thought the jarred sauce was "a bit underwhelming" but that she "loved the crispy texture" overall. Heiskell thought the chicken breast "was a little too dry."

*   **Juicy Roast Chicken**: The judges were impressed by how juicy this chicken was. "It's easy to hide behind a dry wing or thigh, but you can't do that with the breast," explained Heiskell. "The seasoning on the outside definitely got all the way through, she continued. Akorede thought the recipe called for too much onion powder, but he was impressed by the crispiness of the skin. Boyd sayid that the chicken was definitely juicy, "but basic."

texts.6:
# The Best Chicken Recipe of 2023 Is "Perfectly Fried"

As the judges were deliberating, Heiskell had some concerns about whether or not the panko-Parmesan was doing all of the heavy lifting for the Chicken Parmesan. Was it really a fair matchup? Because of this, she decided to cast her vote for the Juicy Roasted Chicken, but the other two judges—Boyd and Akorede—went for the **Chicken Parmesan**, making it our winning recipe for 2023.

# The Best Bacon Recipe on Our Site This Year, According to Fans
_**Best Recipes 2023**: Allrecipes asked our readers and a panel of judges to help us find the best recipe in five different categories: bacon, chicken, potatoes, cheese, and chocolate._**_See the full list of winners here_**_, and read more about the best bacon recipe below._
For the first time ever, Allrecipes has itself a definitive _best_ bacon recipe.
Back in June, the Allrecipes team took on the challenge of finding the best recipe on our site. But, as the largest food site on the internet with over 55,000 recipes, we decided it was only right to break the recipes into categories (I mean, how can you possibly pit the Best Chocolate Chip Cookie against Creamy au Gratin Potatoes?). So, the five contending categories were: bacon, potatoes, cheese, chicken, and chocolate. We gave you 10 community-favorite recipe options for each category, then asked you to vote on the best of each.
In the bacon bracket, the recipes ranged from corn dishes to cabbage dishes, from pasta salads to savory snacks. But, to be the very best, this dish had to be salty, satisfying, and bring full-force bacon flavor. Thanks to your votes, we were able to narrow the bacon recipe pool down to two delicious finalists. It was up to our judges—Carrie Boyd, Elizabeth Heiskell, and Dakari Akorede—to pick the winner.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The Best Bacon Recipe on Our Site This Year, According to Fans
## Meet the Two Contenders
In our inaugural Best Recipe Cook-Off, we had two of our talented recipe testers, Jasmine Smith and Julia Levy, battle it out between the top two bacon recipes.
**Bacon-Wrapped Jalapeño Poppers**: This recipe comes to us from community member videogator, and was first published on July 25, 2013. The flavorful jalapeño poppers are crispy on the outside, and soft and creamy in the center. Stuffed with two kinds of cheese (cream cheese and sharp Cheddar), the poppers deliver layers of savory, spicy flavor in every bite.
"Wrapped with bacon, these are absolutely the best," says user R Vicente.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
They're easy to make (only four ingredients!), perfectly balanced, and exactly what you want to find on the appetizer table. It doesn't matter if you bake them or grill them—these bacon-wrapped peppers will add a delicious kick to any get-together.
**Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole**: This breakfast casserole from SPezz was first published on November 16, 2014. It's made for morning comfort, combining every element of your favorite breakfast in one flavorful bite. It's savory, satisfying, and best of all, simple.
“I put this together in what felt like 5 minutes,” recipe tester Julia said.
This 5-ingredient wonder can be customized with veggies, herbs, or hot sauce, and it’ll still turn out delicious every time.
Peyton Beckwith/Dotdash Meredith

# The #1 Cheese Recipe of 2023 Is the Creamiest Thing You'll Eat All Year
## Meet the Two Contenders
*   **VELVEETA Down-Home Macaroni and Cheese:**This recipe is from VELVEETA Cheese, and was originally published on April 15, 2013. It has 150 reviews with a 4.5-star rating. It made the running for our Best Recipes 2023 contest because it was voted the best mac and cheese recipe in a recent taste test. Our test kitchen pro Amanda Stanfield, says this recipe gets its creaminess from a mix of VELVEETA cheese and cheddar. But what really puts this recipe over the edge is the buttery, crushed Ritz cracker that you add on top of the pasta before baking.

*   **Cheddar Bay Biscuits:**This recipe comes from Cookie, and was first published on April 4, 1999. The biscuits have over 1,300 reviews with a 4.6-star rating. Our test kitchen pro, Catherine Jesse, says this Red Lobster copycat is filled with lots of cheddar cheese, garlic powder, butter, flour, and a few other seasonings.

Title: The 5 Best Recipes of 2023
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8
For Allrecipes' inaugural Best Recipes contest, we tasked our readers, editors, and a panel of expert judges to name the best recipes of the year.
The internet at large likes to throw around the word "best" a lot. This is the _best_ cheeseburger; this is the _best_ way to store blueberries; this is the _best_ way to cut an onion. We get the appeal! When you're deciding between multiple recipes or techniques, why wouldn't you want the best?
But there's just one problem: Who, exactly, gets to decide what qualifies as the best? Who gets to say what recipe is better than another? This year, for the first time ever, we're letting our editors, readers, and a panel of expert judges make the call. For Allrecipes' inaugural **Best Recipes**competition, we pitted 50 recipes against each other to find the "best" recipe in five different categories: bacon, cheese, chicken, potatoes, and chocolate. We whittled down the list, we consulted our readers (almost 20,000 members of our community weighed in!), we ate our way through plates of chicken Parmesan and rich chocolate pie, and we found our champions.
The five winning recipes below are the result of many months of research culminating in a cook-off at our test kitchen in Birmingham. When we say these recipes are "the best" for 2023, you can rest assured that it's true.
Dotdash Meredith Design

## How We Decided the Best Recipes of 2023
We took a three-prong approach to finding our best recipes for 2023. In the first phase, our editors determined the five ingredient-based categories, and then chose 10 recipes per category that we felt represented what our community is making right now on Allrecipes—whether that’s something highly rated, brimming with comments on Instagram, or very much in the zeitgeist in 2023. It didn't matter when the recipes were published.
In the second phase, we kicked off a month-long campaign where we asked our readers to vote for their favorite recipes in each category. We had an incredible 111,554 votes from 17,255 voters (with a $1000 cash prize for voting).
The top two recipes in each category went to a cook-off in our test kitchen in Birmingham, Alabama where our panel of judges—Carrie Boyd, Elizabeth Heiskell, and Dakari Akored—tried all 10 recipes, gave their notes, deliberated amongst themselves, and declared one winner per category.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Meet the Judges
For our cook-off in Birmingham, we brought in three top-tier judges to make the final call on the best recipes of 2023. Let's meet the team!
*   **Elizabeth Heiskell**: Heiskell is a _The Today Show_ Food Contributor and has appeared on both _The Kitchen_ and _Chopped_. She's also the best-selling cookbook author of _What Can I Bring_, _The Southern Living Party Cookbook_, and _Come On Over_. She lives in Oxford, Mississippi where she runs her catering company, Elizabeth Heiskell Catering.  
*   **Dakari Akorede**: Akorede is an Allrecipes' Allstar, a football fan, and a BBQ expert. He lives in Atlanta and works as a private chef and teacher.  
*   **Carrie Boyd**: Boyd is the Editorial Director for _Allrecipes_ magazine. She has more than a decade of experience in national food and lifestyle media and content creation. In another life, she created custom, branded content for national brands; and worked in various FOH and BOH jobs in the hospitality industry. She lives in Iowa.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## The Best Recipes 2023 Cook-Off
When it comes to the vibe of our cook-off in Birmingham on July 26, think: _Top Chef_ meets the home cook. In typical TV fashion, our judges sat on a long table, with fork and pen in hand, ready to eat and take notes. Our test kitchen chefs made and served our judges each recipe while telling them a little bit about the history of the dish on the site. Allrecipes is built on the recipes from our contributors, so it was a joy to hear about the cook behind the dish, and when it was published on our site (a couple were from 1999!). The judges in turn tried each recipe, gave their notes, and voted on the ultimate winner. Here's how the whole thing shook out.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Bacon: Not Just a Morning Hero
**The Contenders**: **Bacon-Wrapped Jalapeño Poppers** vs. **Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole**
Our test kitchen chefs, Jasmine Smith and Julia Levy, made and served both of these recipes to our judges. The poppers had thick-cut bacon wrapped around the outside of the pepper, while the casserole has bacon throughout and on top of the dish. The judges swooned over the poppers, and Akorede said the recipe was "savory, salty, with just a small twinge of heat". But ultimately, **the casserole reigned supreme**. Boyd described it as “the perfect marriage" of an egg casserole and a hot dish. “I have no notes here,” she said, "10/10."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Potatoes: The Queen of Comfort
**The Contenders**: **Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes** vs. **Creamy au Gratin Potatoes**
For our potato category, our test kitchen pros Amanda Stanfield and Catherine Jesse made and served our judges. The baked potatoes were a twice-baked potato filled with bacon, cheddar, sour cream, and green onions. The gratin potatoes used thinly-sliced potatoes as the base. The judges thought that the potatoes in the gratin were perfectly cooked, but Akorede thought the "onions were too sharp." **The baked potato stole the show**. "This [recipe] makes me think about home," Akorede said.
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Cheese: The Secret to Making Everything Better
**The Contenders**: **VELVEETA Down-Home Macaroni and Cheese** vs. **Cheddar Bay Biscuits**
Stanfield and Jesse came back to make and serve the recipes for the cheese category to our judges. The macaroni and cheese used two kinds of cheeses for superior creaminess—VELVEETA and cheddar. And the Red Lobster copycat biscuits used grated cheddar to impart cheesiness throughout. While the judges thought the biscuits were "light and savory" they also thought they were a tad bit dry. **The macaroni and cheese**, on the other hand, was "creamy and delicious" according to Heiskell, making it our #1 cheese recipe of 2023.
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Chicken: A Kitchen Bedrock
**The Contenders**: **Chicken Parmesan** vs. **Juicy Roast Chicken**
Our test kitchen chefs, Nicole Hopper and Tricia Stuedeman, made and served our judges for the chicken category. The roast chicken is a fuss-free recipe with superior results, and the chicken Parmesan uses a mixture of panko and Parmesan for ultimate crispiness. Heiskell thought the roast chicken was incredibly juicy. "It's easy to hide behind a dry wing or thigh, but you can't do that with the breast," she said. **But Boyd and Akorede preferred the chicken Parmesan, making it our winner**. Akorede said it was a "great dish" and that the chicken was "perfectly fried."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

## Chocolate: The Sweetest Way to End the Day
**The Contenders: Rich Chocolate Truffle Pie** vs. **One Bowl Chocolate Cake**
Stuedeman and Hopper also made and served the chocolate recipes to our judges. The cake uses unsweetened cocoa powder, while the pie utilized semisweet chocolate chips and a chocolate cookie crumb crust. Heiskell thought the cake was a "lovely rich and moist cake," **but it didn't hold a candle to the pie**. Akorede's eyes rolled to the back of his head while declaring that the pie was "absolutely phenomenal."
Read more about both recipes and what the judges had to say.

We have over 5,000 chicken recipes on Allrecipes—so it's safe to say our community loves its poultry. To find the best chicken recipe of the year, our editors looked at our library and chose 10 recipes that were beloved by our readers and/or were popular on the internet right now. # The Best Chicken Recipe of 2023 Is "Perfectly Fried"
## Meet the Two Contenders
*   **Chicken Parmesan**: This recipe was published by Chef John on June 6, 2012. It has over 3,200 reviews with a 4.7-star rating. It's also our top chicken recipe of the past 12 months. Test kitchen pro Nicole Hopper told our judges that this recipe is "very straightforward" but that it's a less-saucy version than some might be used to. Hopper said this was great because it helped avoid that dreaded soggy-bottom chicken. She also notes that the recipe uses three kinds of cheese: mozzarella, provolone, and Parmesan.

*   **Juicy Roast Chicken**: ROBINROCKINGBIRD published this recipe on May 4, 2005. It has over 3,100 reviews with a 4.7-star rating, and it was our third most popular chicken recipe of the past 12 months. Our test kitchen pro, Tricia Stuedeman, says this recipe lives up to its name—it's ultra juicy. The chicken also roasts at one temperature the entire time, making it pretty fuss-free.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The Best Chicken Recipe of 2023 Is "Perfectly Fried"
## What the Judges Had to Say
*   **Chicken Parmesan**: Akorede loved this recipe immediately. "It's a great dish, perfectly fried chicken with the added sweetness of the sauce and cheese," he said. Boyd thought the jarred sauce was "a bit underwhelming" but that she "loved the crispy texture" overall. Heiskell thought the chicken breast "was a little too dry."

*   **Juicy Roast Chicken**: The judges were impressed by how juicy this chicken was. "It's easy to hide behind a dry wing or thigh, but you can't do that with the breast," explained Heiskell. "The seasoning on the outside definitely got all the way through, she continued. Akorede thought the recipe called for too much onion powder, but he was impressed by the crispiness of the skin. Boyd sayid that the chicken was definitely juicy, "but basic."
Dotdash Meredith Food Studio

# The Best Chicken Recipe of 2023 Is "Perfectly Fried"
## And the Winner Is...
As the judges were deliberating, Heiskell had some concerns about whether or not the panko-Parmesan was doing all of the heavy lifting for the Chicken Parmesan. Was it really a fair matchup? Because of this, she decided to cast her vote for the Juicy Roasted Chicken, but the other two judges—Boyd and Akorede—went for the **Chicken Parmesan**, making it our winning recipe for 2023.

# The Best Bacon Recipe on Our Site This Year, According to Fans
_**Best Recipes 2023**: Allrecipes asked our readers and a panel of judges to help us find the best recipe in five different categories: bacon, chicken, potatoes, cheese, and chocolate._**_See the full list of winners here_**_, and read more about the best bacon recipe below._
For the first time ever, Allrecipes has itself a definitive _best_ bacon recipe.
Back in June, the Allrecipes team took on the challenge of finding the best recipe on our site. But, as the largest food site on the internet with over 55,000 recipes, we decided it was only right to break the recipes into categories (I mean, how can you possibly pit the Best Chocolate Chip Cookie against Creamy au Gratin Potatoes?). So, the five contending categories were: bacon, potatoes, cheese, chicken, and chocolate. We gave you 10 community-favorite recipe options for each category, then asked you to vote on the best of each.
In the bacon bracket, the recipes ranged from corn dishes to cabbage dishes, from pasta salads to savory snacks. But, to be the very best, this dish had to be salty, satisfying, and bring full-force bacon flavor. Thanks to your votes, we were able to narrow the bacon recipe pool down to two delicious finalists. It was up to our judges—Carrie Boyd, Elizabeth Heiskell, and Dakari Akorede—to pick the winner.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios

# The Best Bacon Recipe on Our Site This Year, According to Fans
## Meet the Two Contenders
In our inaugural Best Recipe Cook-Off, we had two of our talented recipe testers, Jasmine Smith and Julia Levy, battle it out between the top two bacon recipes.
**Bacon-Wrapped Jalapeño Poppers**: This recipe comes to us from community member videogator, and was first published on July 25, 2013. The flavorful jalapeño poppers are crispy on the outside, and soft and creamy in the center. Stuffed with two kinds of cheese (cream cheese and sharp Cheddar), the poppers deliver layers of savory, spicy flavor in every bite.
"Wrapped with bacon, these are absolutely the best," says user R Vicente.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
They're easy to make (only four ingredients!), perfectly balanced, and exactly what you want to find on the appetizer table. It doesn't matter if you bake them or grill them—these bacon-wrapped peppers will add a delicious kick to any get-together.
**Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole**: This breakfast casserole from SPezz was first published on November 16, 2014. It's made for morning comfort, combining every element of your favorite breakfast in one flavorful bite. It's savory, satisfying, and best of all, simple.
“I put this together in what felt like 5 minutes,” recipe tester Julia said.
This 5-ingredient wonder can be customized with veggies, herbs, or hot sauce, and it’ll still turn out delicious every time.
Peyton Beckwith/Dotdash Meredith

# The Best Bacon Recipe on Our Site This Year, According to Fans
## What the Judges Had to Say
*   **Bacon-Wrapped Jalapeño Poppers**: "Yummmm, exactly what I want tailgating," says Boyd. "The cheddar addition is tasty and different." Akorede agreed, saying "The contrast—the cream cheese in conjunction with the bacon—you can’t beat it." Heiskell said although the peppers were roasted perfectly, bacon was the star of this dish: "It was the first thing I saw."

*   **Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole:** “You know, I make a breakfast casserole, and I have for years, but I have to say, this one is on a whole 'nother level. This has got everything—it has the bacon, and then the tater tots! I mean, come on! Who does that?,” raved Heiskell. Boyd said it was “the perfect marriage” of an egg casserole and a hot dish. “I have no notes here,” she said, "10/10."
Peyton Beckwith/Dotdash Meredith

# The Best Bacon Recipe on Our Site This Year, According to Fans
## And the Winner Is...
The **Tater Tot and Bacon Breakfast Casserole**!
We love bacon in almost every application, but everybody knows bacon’s main stage is the breakfast table. So, it's only right that our top bacon recipe pairs salty, smoky bacon with its best breakfast counterparts.
The judges loved how the bacon flavor melded with the eggs, hash browns, and cheese to make a top-notch breakfast feast. Recipe tester Julia also gave her casserole over-the-top bacon flavor by finishing it off with salty bacon crumbles, ultimately earning it the gold.
Not only is this recipe delicious, but it’s our bacon champion because it’s so simple and dependable, proving that “basic” is hard to beat. With crowd-favorite flavors and a fuss-free preparation, this is a recipe to keep in your back pocket year-round.

Cheese is the literal magic sauce in our mac and cheese, the tour de force in our enchiladas, and the wind beneath (or on top of) our pizza. That's why when we attempted to find the best cheese recipe for Allrecipes' Best Recipes 2023 competition, we took the task very seriously. # The #1 Cheese Recipe of 2023 Is the Creamiest Thing You'll Eat All Year
## Meet the Two Contenders
*   **VELVEETA Down-Home Macaroni and Cheese:**This recipe is from VELVEETA Cheese, and was originally published on April 15, 2013. It has 150 reviews with a 4.5-star rating. It made the running for our Best Recipes 2023 contest because it was voted the best mac and cheese recipe in a recent taste test. Our test kitchen pro Amanda Stanfield, says this recipe gets its creaminess from a mix of VELVEETA cheese and cheddar. But what really puts this recipe over the edge is the buttery, crushed Ritz cracker that you add on top of the pasta before baking.

*   **Cheddar Bay Biscuits:**This recipe comes from Cookie, and was first published on April 4, 1999. The biscuits have over 1,300 reviews with a 4.6-star rating. Our test kitchen pro, Catherine Jesse, says this Red Lobster copycat is filled with lots of cheddar cheese, garlic powder, butter, flour, and a few other seasonings.

*   **VELVEETA Down-Home Macaroni and Cheese:** Boyd said this macaroni and cheese was "creamy, cheesy, and so tasty!" And that she loved the buttery Ritz crackers on top. # The #1 Cheese Recipe of 2023 Is the Creamiest Thing You'll Eat All Year

## How to Store Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
Cover the tater tot breakfast casserole, then store it in the refrigerator for up to one week. Reheat in the microwave or in the oven.

Yes, this tater tot and bacon casserole freezes well for up to three months. Reheat from frozen in the oven until the casserole is heated through.

*   cooking spray

*   1 pound bacon

*   1 pound bulk pork sausage

*   3 ½ cups frozen bite-sized potato nuggets (such as Tater Tots®)

*   ½ cup unsalted butter, melted

*   3 cups grated Colby-Jack cheese, divided

*   8 large eggs

*   2 cups milk

*   1 small onion, chopped

*   1 ½ tablespoons prepared yellow mustard

*   salt and ground black pepper to taste

# Cheesy Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
## Directions
1.   Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Spray a 9x12-inch baking dish with cooking spray.

   
2.   Place bacon in a large skillet and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain bacon slices on paper towels and let cool.

   
3.   Heat the same skillet over medium-high heat and add sausage. Cook and stir until browned and crumbly, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove from heat. Crumble cooled bacon.

   
4.   Place potato nuggets in the bottom of the prepared baking dish, distributed evenly. Drizzle evenly with melted butter. Sprinkle with 1 1/2 cups of Colby-Jack cheese.

   
5.   Mix eggs, milk, onion, 1/2 of the bacon and sausage, mustard, salt, and pepper together in a bowl. Pour into the baking dish. Add remaining Colby-Jack cheese, bacon, and sausage.

   
6.   Bake in the preheated oven until set and cheese is melted, about 1 hour. Let cool for 15 minutes before serving.

# Cheesy Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
## Editor's Note:
Please note the omission of butter, as well as a slight difference in adding the milk mixture when using the magazine version of this recipe.

*   1(32 ounce) bag frozen tater tots

*   1 pound breakfast sausage, cooked and crumbled

*   8 slices bacon, cooked and crumbled

*   8 ounces Colby Jack cheese, shredded

*   6 medium green onions, sliced, divided

*   8 large eggs

*   2 cups whole milk

*   2 teaspoons hot sauce

*   1 teaspoon kosher salt

*   1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper

# Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
## Directions
1.   Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (180 degrees C).

   
2.   Add tater tots to the bottom of a deep 9x13-inch baking dish and top evenly with sausage, bacon, and cheese.

   
3.   Reserve 3 tablespoons green onions, and sprinkle remaining onions over cheese.

   
4.   Combine eggs, milk, hot sauce, salt, and pepper in a food processor and mix until well blended, about 10 seconds. Pour egg mixture over tater tot mixture.

   
5.   Bake in the preheated oven until set and browned around the edges, about 50 minutes; cover during the last 20 minutes loosely with foil if too much browning occurs before casserole sets. Let stand for 10 minutes before serving and serve topped with reserved green onions.

# Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
## Photos of Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
The main photo on this recipe does not represent how this casserole is assembled. The photo shows tots on the top. The recipe instructs you to put the tater tots on the bottom as the first layer, and there’s no way they’re going to float to the top. What you end up with are mushy potatoes from the egg custard instead of crisp tots. As written, I really think regular cubed potatoes would have worked just as well on the bottom. I followed this recipe to the letter and after 50 minutes, it appeared nicely browned around the edges, and I took it out of the oven. After letting it sit for 10 minutes, I tried to cut it into squares, but it was too soupy to do so. I bumped up the temp to 400ºF, covered with foil, back in the oven for 10 minutes, removed the foil, and baked for another 5 minutes, so I could cut into squares. I have to wonder if this recipe needs less milk and eggs or if it needs to be cooked at a higher temperature…IDK. This ended up looking like many, many other breakfast casseroles, not a tater tot casserole. Had the tots been on the top, I would think they’d have been somewhat crispy and with a lot more eye appeal. We really enjoyed the flavor, so I will try this again putting tater tots on the top instead of the bottom. Sorry for the long review.

# Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
## Photos of Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
The main photo on this recipe does not represent how this casserole is assembled. The photo shows tots on the top. The recipe instructs you to put the tater tots on the bottom as the first layer, and there’s no way they’re going to float to the top. What you end up with are mushy potatoes from the egg custard instead of crisp tots. As written, I really think regular cubed potatoes would have worked just as well on the bottom. I followed this recipe to the letter and after 50 minutes, it appeared nicely browned around the edges, and I took it out of the oven. After letting it sit for 10 minutes, I tried to cut it into squares, but it was too soupy to do so. I bumped up the temp to 400ºF, covered with foil, back in the oven for 10 minutes, removed the foil, and baked for another 5 minutes, so I could cut into squares. I have to wonder if this recipe needs less milk and eggs or if it needs to be cooked at a higher temperature…IDK. This ended up looking like many, many other breakfast casseroles, not a tater tot casserole. Had the tots been on the top, I would think they’d have been somewhat crispy and with a lot more eye appeal. We really enjoyed the flavor, so I will try this again putting tater tots on the top instead of the bottom. Sorry for the long review.

texts.5:
# Cheesy Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
## Directions
1.   Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Spray a 9x12-inch baking dish with cooking spray.

   
2.   Place bacon in a large skillet and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain bacon slices on paper towels and let cool.

   
3.   Heat the same skillet over medium-high heat and add sausage. Cook and stir until browned and crumbly, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove from heat. Crumble cooled bacon.

   
4.   Place potato nuggets in the bottom of the prepared baking dish, distributed evenly. Drizzle evenly with melted butter. Sprinkle with 1 1/2 cups of Colby-Jack cheese.

   
5.   Mix eggs, milk, onion, 1/2 of the bacon and sausage, mustard, salt, and pepper together in a bowl. Pour into the baking dish. Add remaining Colby-Jack cheese, bacon, and sausage.

   
6.   Bake in the preheated oven until set and cheese is melted, about 1 hour. Let cool for 15 minutes before serving.

The main photo on this recipe does not represent how this casserole is assembled. The photo shows tots on the top. The recipe instructs you to put the tater tots on the bottom as the first layer, and there’s no way they’re going to float to the top. *   cooking spray

*   1 pound bacon

*   1 pound bulk pork sausage

*   3 ½ cups frozen bite-sized potato nuggets (such as Tater Tots®)

*   ½ cup unsalted butter, melted

*   3 cups grated Colby-Jack cheese, divided

*   8 large eggs

*   2 cups milk

*   1 small onion, chopped

*   1 ½ tablespoons prepared yellow mustard

*   salt and ground black pepper to taste

# Cheesy Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
## Directions
1.   Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Spray a 9x12-inch baking dish with cooking spray.

   
2.   Place bacon in a large skillet and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain bacon slices on paper towels and let cool.

   
3.   Heat the same skillet over medium-high heat and add sausage. Cook and stir until browned and crumbly, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove from heat. Crumble cooled bacon.

   
4.   Place potato nuggets in the bottom of the prepared baking dish, distributed evenly. Drizzle evenly with melted butter. Sprinkle with 1 1/2 cups of Colby-Jack cheese.

   
5.   Mix eggs, milk, onion, 1/2 of the bacon and sausage, mustard, salt, and pepper together in a bowl. Pour into the baking dish. Add remaining Colby-Jack cheese, bacon, and sausage.

   
6.   Bake in the preheated oven until set and cheese is melted, about 1 hour. Let cool for 15 minutes before serving.

# Cheesy Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
## Editor's Note:
Please note the omission of butter, as well as a slight difference in adding the milk mixture when using the magazine version of this recipe.

*   canola oil cooking spray

*   ½ cup water

*   1 egg, beaten

*   1 ½ cups bread crumbs

*   6 tablespoons grated Parmesan cheese, divided

*   1 tablespoon dried oregano

*   1 teaspoon dried basil

*   ½ teaspoon dried thyme

*   ½ teaspoon garlic powder

*   6 skinless, boneless chicken breasts

*   2 cups spaghetti sauce

*   1 cup shredded mozzarella cheese

# Quick Baked Chicken Parmesan
## Directions
1.   Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Coat a 9x13-inch baking dish with cooking spray.

   
2.   Whisk water and egg together in a bowl until smooth. Combine bread crumbs, 2 tablespoons Parmesan cheese, oregano, basil, thyme, and garlic powder in a separate bowl.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
3.   Dip each chicken breast, one at a time, into beaten egg mixture; lift up so excess egg mixture drips back into bowl. Place each chicken breast, one at a time, in bread crumb mixture; press to coat, then shake off excess.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
4.   Repeat dipping and coating each coated chicken breast in egg mixture followed by bread crumb mixture for a double-coating; place breasts in the prepared baking dish. Coat breasts with cooking spray.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
5.   Bake in the preheated oven for 40 minutes.

   
6.   Pour spaghetti sauce over each breast; top each with mozzarella cheese and remaining 4 tablespoons Parmesan cheese.
Dotdash Meredith Food Studios
7.   Continue baking until chicken no longer pink in centers and cheeses are melted, about 15 minutes more. An instant-read thermometer inserted into centers should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

   
8.   Serve over pasta.
DOTDASH MEREDITH FOOD STUDIOS

## Healthy Chicken Parmesan Recipe
4.99 from 52 votes
This Baked Chicken Parmesan recipe is so easy to make! Perfectly crispy, coated with a delicious sauce and cheese for a healthy dinner!
Prep Time : 20 minutes
Cook Time : 35 minutes
Total Time : 55 minutes
Serves : 4 people (about 1 chicken cutlet each)
*   1½ pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts  
*   ½ cupwhole wheat flour  
*   3 large eggs  
*   1 cup whole wheat breadcrumbs unseasoned  
*   ½ cup grated Parmesan  
*   ¼ teaspoon black pepper  
*   2 teaspoons dried basil  
*   2 teaspoons dried parsley  
*   1½ cupsmarinara sauce  
*   1½ cups shredded mozzarella
1.   Butterfly the chicken by slicing the chicken breasts in half lengthwise (like a book). Place the chicken in between plastic wrap and use a meat mallet to pound the chicken until it is about ¼-inch thick. This is important, as skipping this step will result in undercooked, tough chicken. You should have 6 cutlets when finished butterflying.

2.   Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F and prepare a parchment-lined baking sheet.

3.   Set out 3 large shallow bowls.

4.   In the first bowl, add the flour.

5.   In the second bowl, crack and whisk the eggs

6.   In the third bowl, mix together breadcrumbs, Parmesan, pepper, basil, and parsley.

7.   Form an assembly line with your bowls. Take the chicken cutlet and cover in the flour, then dip in the egg, then dip in the breadcrumb mixture. Press gently to make sure the cutlets are coated. Repeat for all the cutlets.

8.   Place breaded cutlets on a baking sheet. Bake at 425 for 15 minutes, then flip the cutlets and bake for another 15 minutes.

9.   After the chicken has been baking for 30 minutes, top each cutlet with about ¼ cup tomato sauce and ¼ cup shredded mozzarella. Return to the oven and set to broil for about 2 minutes until the cheese is melted.

10.   Serve over pasta or a salad.

## Healthy Chicken Parmesan Recipe
4.99 from 52 votes
This Baked Chicken Parmesan recipe is so easy to make! Perfectly crispy, coated with a delicious sauce and cheese for a healthy dinner!
Prep Time : 20 minutes
Cook Time : 35 minutes
Total Time : 55 minutes
Serves : 4 people (about 1 chicken cutlet each)
*   1½ pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts  
*   ½ cupwhole wheat flour  
*   3 large eggs  
*   1 cup whole wheat breadcrumbs unseasoned  
*   ½ cup grated Parmesan  
*   ¼ teaspoon black pepper  
*   2 teaspoons dried basil  
*   2 teaspoons dried parsley  
*   1½ cupsmarinara sauce  
*   1½ cups shredded mozzarella
1.   Butterfly the chicken by slicing the chicken breasts in half lengthwise (like a book). Place the chicken in between plastic wrap and use a meat mallet to pound the chicken until it is about ¼-inch thick. This is important, as skipping this step will result in undercooked, tough chicken. You should have 6 cutlets when finished butterflying.

2.   Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F and prepare a parchment-lined baking sheet.

3.   Set out 3 large shallow bowls.

4.   In the first bowl, add the flour.

5.   In the second bowl, crack and whisk the eggs

6.   In the third bowl, mix together breadcrumbs, Parmesan, pepper, basil, and parsley.

7.   Form an assembly line with your bowls. Take the chicken cutlet and cover in the flour, then dip in the egg, then dip in the breadcrumb mixture. Press gently to make sure the cutlets are coated. Repeat for all the cutlets.

8.   Place breaded cutlets on a baking sheet. Bake at 425 for 15 minutes, then flip the cutlets and bake for another 15 minutes.

9.   After the chicken has been baking for 30 minutes, top each cutlet with about ¼ cup tomato sauce and ¼ cup shredded mozzarella. Return to the oven and set to broil for about 2 minutes until the cheese is melted.

10.   Serve over pasta or a salad.

## Velveeta Mac and Cheese
If you’re looking for the creamy mac and cheese of your childhood, this is it.
Serves
4.61 from 274 votes
Prep Time 5 minutes
Cook Time 20 minutes
Total Time 25 minutes
*   8 oz macaroni about 2 cups dry, or other small pasta of choice, half a 1lb box  
*   2 tbsp butter  
*   2 tbsp flour  
*   1/2 tsp garlic powder  
*   1/2 tsp onion powder  
*   1/2 tsp dry mustard powder  
*   1.5 cups milk of choice  
*   1/2 lb Velveeta cheese cubed  
*   1/2 cup shredded cheddar

*   Cook the macaroni in a large pot of salted water according to the package directions. Save a cup of pasta water, then drain well.

*   In a large saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. When melted, stir in the flour, garlic powder, onion powder, and dry mustard, until smooth and incorporated.

*   Pour the milk into the pan in a thin stream while whisking, until smooth. Keep on medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the sauce bubbles and thickens, 3-5 minutes.

*   Turn the heat to low, add the cubed Velveeta and shredded cheddar and stir until melted and creamy.

*   Add in the drained macaroni, mixing until evenly coated, taste and season with salt and pepper. Loosen with pasta water if needed. Enjoy!
To bake: Cook the pasta 2 minutes less than the package and add an extra 1/4 cup of milk to the sauce. Scoop the mac and cheese into a oven safe casserole dish, top with 1/4 cup of shredded cheddar and 1/4 cup panko breadcrumbs or crushed ritz crackers and bake at 350°F until the cheese melts and is golden and crisp, 20-30 minutes.

If you’re looking for the creamy mac and cheese of your childhood, this is it.

4.61 from 274 votes

*   8 oz macaroni about 2 cups dry, or other small pasta of choice, half a 1lb box  
*   2 tbsp butter

*   1/2 tsp onion powder  
*   1/2 tsp dry mustard powder  
*   1.5 cups milk of choice  
*   1/2 lb Velveeta cheese cubed  
*   1/2 cup shredded cheddar

*   Cook the macaroni in a large pot of salted water according to the package directions. Save a cup of pasta water, then drain well.

*   In a large saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. When melted, stir in the flour, garlic powder, onion powder, and dry mustard, until smooth and incorporated.

*   Pour the milk into the pan in a thin stream while whisking, until smooth. Keep on medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the sauce bubbles and thickens, 3-5 minutes.

*   Turn the heat to low, add the cubed Velveeta and shredded cheddar and stir until melted and creamy.

*   Add in the drained macaroni, mixing until evenly coated, taste and season with salt and pepper. Loosen with pasta water if needed. Enjoy!

Asked by Elsa
Why is my twice-baked potato filling so sticky?
View Answers (7)
Two issues come to mind. The first is over mixing. When you are first handling the baked potato flesh, remember you will be stirring in more ingredients, and the more potatoes are stirred, the more likely they develop the strands of starch that we notice as stickiness. With all the yummy add-ins, they don't need to be perfectly smooth. The second is to make sure you are using Russet potatoes, and not one of the waxy varieties, such as red or yellow potatoes.
By Bibi
When you over mix potatoes they become gummy and sticky. Using a potato ricer or food mill will help a lot. Also it's fine for them to not be emulsified.
By SpeedyFork7536
Not enough moisture or over whipping. Russets..only use them. I add cold butter, half n half, sour cream and mix. It’s perfectly ok to have small potato chunks.. Stir in cheese, onion, S&P, bacon. Stuff the skins, then heat in oven, not microwave. Toward serving time, top with cheese and green onions. Do not skimp on salt! Potatoes are extremely bland with not enough salt

Do NOT use a mixer!!! Only use a potato masher and you will be just fine. I've made them for years and never had a fail.

*   4 large baking potatoes

*   ½ pound bacon

*   4 tablespoons butter

*   1 large onion, chopped

*   ½ cup chopped fresh mushrooms

*   1 teaspoon crushed red pepper

*   1 teaspoon garlic powder

*   1 teaspoon ground black pepper

*   1 teaspoon chopped fresh chives

*   1 teaspoon salt

*   1(8 ounce) container sour cream

*   1(8 ounce) package shredded Cheddar cheese

*   1 teaspoon dry bread crumbs

# Twice Baked Potatoes
## Directions
1.   Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Use a fork to pierce the potato skins.

   
2.   Bake the potatoes unwrapped for about 1 hour, or until soft, in the preheated oven.

   
3.   Place bacon in a large, deep skillet. Cook over medium high heat until evenly brown. Drain, crumble and set aside.

   
4.   Over medium-low heat melt the butter in a large saucepan. Combine onion, mushrooms, red pepper, garlic powder, pepper, chives and salt. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally until the onions are soft.

   
5.   Slice open the baked potatoes and, keeping the skins intact, scoop the insides into a medium bowl. Transfer the onion mixture to the bowl. Mix in the sour cream. Pour in 1/2 of the cheese and continue mixing until all ingredients are well blended.

   
6.   Using a large spoon, fill the potato skins with the mixture. Top with bread crumbs, the remaining cheese and bacon.

   
7.   Return the potatoes to the preheated oven and continue baking for about 15 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the filling is slightly brown.

Easy, Healthier, Twice Baked Potatoes
opened.information:
Source: https://heathermangieri.com/low-fat-simple-twice-baked-potato/
Title: Easy, Healthier, Twice Baked Potatoes
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4
_**This creamy on the inside, crunchy on the outside twice-baked potatoes recipe is so easy to prepare, and packed full of potassium, fiber and vitamin C.**_
Roasted, baked, mashed, fried – there are so many delicious ways to prepare potatoes. The one that’s often forgotten is my personal favorite, the twice-baked potato.
Though potatoes have a bad reputation, don’t let their white flesh fool you. Potatoes are a leading source of potassium in the American diet, and a great source of vitamin C and fiber. Most importantly, they are a vegetable well-accepted by kids. As a mom, I can tell you, mealtime is much more enjoyable when the kids like what you serve.
As with any vegetable, it’s the preparation method that can make it or break it. Most twice-baked potato recipes exceed the recommendations of dietary fat _per serving_. Higher-fat means higher calorie – but that doesn’t mean you can’t enjoy this dish as part of a healthy lifestyle.

### _**Healthy Swaps To Make Twice-Baked Potatoes Healthier**_
With just a few alterations, I transitioned the recipe of traditional twice-baked potatoes into a lower-calorie, lower-fat version that can fit into any calorie level.
I usually don’t recommend fat free products, but this recipe is an exception. I used fat-free sour cream in the potato mixture. It works well when prepared in a mixture like this because it created the creamy texture without adding a lot of dietary fat. I was also careful with the portion size of each of the ingredients that I used. Each potato is topped with ~2 tablespoons of cheddar cheese, which is absolutely enough to get the flavor. And, of course, chives!

### _**Calories And Nutrition Information**_
The nutrition information provided if for one serving, or one ~6 ounce twice baked potato. That’s 1/2 of a large potato, cut in half. When prepared as described, one twice baked potato has 240 calories, 4.5 grams of fat, 3 grams of saturated fat, 15 milligrams of cholesterol, 42 grams of carbohydrates, 4 grams of fiber and 8 grams of protein. It also has 180 milligrams of sodium, 30% ofthe daily value for vitamin C,10% of the daily value for iron, 15% of the daily value for calcium and 20% of the daily value for potassium. That makes this side dish a highly nutritious option!
These twice baked potatoes are absolutely amazing and are a great way to mix-up your dinner side dish options. Give them a try and let me know what you think.
If you love twice-baked potatoes, you might also like my recipe for twice baked sweet potatoes with rosemary and ricotta.

## Low-Fat Simple Twice Baked Potatoes
_**This creamy on the inside, crunchy on the outside twice-baked potato recipe is so easy to prepare, and packed full of potassium, fiber and vitamin C.**_
Author: Heather Mangieri, RDN
*   2 Large Potatoes  
*   2 Slices of Bacon (microwaved)  
*   3/4 cup Fat Free Sour Cream  
*   1/2 cup Non-Fat Milk  
*   1/4 cup Shredded Cheddar Cheese  
*   1 tbsp Butter (salted)  
*   4 tbsp Fresh Chives (chopped)

*   Pre-heat oven to 375 degrees. Wrap 2 large (10-12 ounce potatoes) in aluminum foil. Bake in the oven at 375 degrees until done, ~1 ½ hours. Let cool completely. (I recommend baking the potatoes the day before and letting them cool in the refrigerator overnight.)

*   Using a sharp knife, cut the potatoes in half lengthwise. Scrape out the inside of the potato, being careful not to tear the skin. Place the inside potato in a bowl. Lay the hollowed potato shell in a glass baking dish or sheet pan.

*   Melt the 1 tbsp. butter in the microwave then add it to the potato that was scooped out of the shell. Use a fork to mash the potatoes well. Add the fat-free sour cream and the milk. Add one piece of the crumbled bacon, 2 tbsp. chopped chives and 1/8 of the shredded cheese to the potato mixture. Continue mixing well.

*   Spoon the potato mixture into the potato shells, evenly distributing between the 4 shells. Once filled (they should be heaping with potato filling,) sprinkle the remaining cheddar cheese, chives and bacon on top of the filling.

*   Place in the oven and bake at 350 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until the cheese is bubbling and the tops are crispy. Top with a tbsp. of fat-free sour cream before serving.

## Low-Fat Simple Twice Baked Potatoes
*   **Makes 4 (~6 ounce) twice-baked potatoes**  
*   **Nutrition Facts**: 1 (~6 ounce) twice baked potato= 240 calories; 4.5 g fat, 3 g saturated fat, 15 mg cholesterol, 42 g carbohydrates, 4 g fiber, 8 g protein, 180 mg sodium, 30% DV Vitamin C, 10% DV iron, 15% DV calcium, 20% DV potassium  
*   Nutrition Tip- for those on a lower-calorie meal plan, cut one twice-baked potato in half for a ~3 ounce serving  
*   Meal Planning Serving Sizes: **3 CHO; 1 FAT; 1.5 PRO**
**DID YOU MAKE THIS RECIPE?**Tag @heathermangieri on Instagram and hashtag it #HeatherMangieriNutrition to show me your creation. Or, Pin it on Pinterest for later!

# Ultimate Twice-Baked Potatoes
## Ask the Community (19)
Asked by Elsa
Why is my twice-baked potato filling so sticky?
View Answers (7)
Two issues come to mind. The first is over mixing. When you are first handling the baked potato flesh, remember you will be stirring in more ingredients, and the more potatoes are stirred, the more likely they develop the strands of starch that we notice as stickiness. With all the yummy add-ins, they don't need to be perfectly smooth. The second is to make sure you are using Russet potatoes, and not one of the waxy varieties, such as red or yellow potatoes.
By Bibi
When you over mix potatoes they become gummy and sticky. Using a potato ricer or food mill will help a lot. Also it's fine for them to not be emulsified.
By SpeedyFork7536
Not enough moisture or over whipping. Russets..only use them. I add cold butter, half n half, sour cream and mix. It’s perfectly ok to have small potato chunks.. Stir in cheese, onion, S&P, bacon. Stuff the skins, then heat in oven, not microwave. Toward serving time, top with cheese and green onions. Do not skimp on salt! Potatoes are extremely bland with not enough salt
By Gerireski
Do NOT use a mixer!!! Only use a potato masher and you will be just fine. I've made them for years and never had a fail.

_**This creamy on the inside, crunchy on the outside twice-baked potatoes recipe is so easy to prepare, and packed full of potassium, fiber and vitamin C.**_
Roasted, baked, mashed, fried – there are so many delicious ways to prepare potatoes. The one that’s often forgotten is my personal favorite, the twice-baked potato.
Though potatoes have a bad reputation, don’t let their white flesh fool you. Potatoes are a leading source of potassium in the American diet, and a great source of vitamin C and fiber. Most importantly, they are a vegetable well-accepted by kids. As a mom, I can tell you, mealtime is much more enjoyable when the kids like what you serve.
As with any vegetable, it’s the preparation method that can make it or break it. Most twice-baked potato recipes exceed the recommendations of dietary fat _per serving_. Higher-fat means higher calorie – but that doesn’t mean you can’t enjoy this dish as part of a healthy lifestyle.
texts.1:
### _**Healthy Swaps To Make Twice-Baked Potatoes Healthier**_
With just a few alterations, I transitioned the recipe of traditional twice-baked potatoes into a lower-calorie, lower-fat version that can fit into any calorie level.
I usually don’t recommend fat free products, but this recipe is an exception. I used fat-free sour cream in the potato mixture. It works well when prepared in a mixture like this because it created the creamy texture without adding a lot of dietary fat. I was also careful with the portion size of each of the ingredients that I used. Each potato is topped with ~2 tablespoons of cheddar cheese, which is absolutely enough to get the flavor. And, of course, chives!
texts.2:
### _**Calories And Nutrition Information**_
The nutrition information provided if for one serving, or one ~6 ounce twice baked potato. That’s 1/2 of a large potato, cut in half. When prepared as described, one twice baked potato has 240 calories, 4.5 grams of fat, 3 grams of saturated fat, 15 milligrams of cholesterol, 42 grams of carbohydrates, 4 grams of fiber and 8 grams of protein. It also has 180 milligrams of sodium, 30% ofthe daily value for vitamin C,10% of the daily value for iron, 15% of the daily value for calcium and 20% of the daily value for potassium. That makes this side dish a highly nutritious option!
These twice baked potatoes are absolutely amazing and are a great way to mix-up your dinner side dish options. Give them a try and let me know what you think.
If you love twice-baked potatoes, you might also like my recipe for twice baked sweet potatoes with rosemary and ricotta.

## Low-Fat Simple Twice Baked Potatoes
_**This creamy on the inside, crunchy on the outside twice-baked potato recipe is so easy to prepare, and packed full of potassium, fiber and vitamin C.**_
Author: Heather Mangieri, RDN
*   2 Large Potatoes  
*   2 Slices of Bacon (microwaved)  
*   3/4 cup Fat Free Sour Cream  
*   1/2 cup Non-Fat Milk  
*   1/4 cup Shredded Cheddar Cheese  
*   1 tbsp Butter (salted)  
*   4 tbsp Fresh Chives (chopped)

*   Pre-heat oven to 375 degrees. Wrap 2 large (10-12 ounce potatoes) in aluminum foil. Bake in the oven at 375 degrees until done, ~1 ½ hours. Let cool completely. (I recommend baking the potatoes the day before and letting them cool in the refrigerator overnight.)

*   Using a sharp knife, cut the potatoes in half lengthwise. Scrape out the inside of the potato, being careful not to tear the skin. Place the inside potato in a bowl. Lay the hollowed potato shell in a glass baking dish or sheet pan.

*   Melt the 1 tbsp. butter in the microwave then add it to the potato that was scooped out of the shell. Use a fork to mash the potatoes well. Add the fat-free sour cream and the milk. Add one piece of the crumbled bacon, 2 tbsp. chopped chives and 1/8 of the shredded cheese to the potato mixture. Continue mixing well.

*   Spoon the potato mixture into the potato shells, evenly distributing between the 4 shells. Once filled (they should be heaping with potato filling,) sprinkle the remaining cheddar cheese, chives and bacon on top of the filling.

*   Place in the oven and bake at 350 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until the cheese is bubbling and the tops are crispy. Top with a tbsp. of fat-free sour cream before serving.

*   4 large baking potatoes

*   1 teaspoon chopped fresh chives
